faqs.q: Does pressure washing or power washing damage roof shingles in East Orange?

runs.v: Yes. Pressure-washing an asphalt shingle roof causes granule loss and premature failure of the roof system, per ARMA, so Newark Quality Roofing uses a low-pressure chemical wash instead.

faqs.q: What removes the dark streaks on a roof in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: The streaks are Gloeocapsa magma algae. The ARMA 50:50 bleach-and-water wash removes them at a 15–20-minute dwell, and the rinse carries off stains and grime, the same approach used for removing mold and mildew.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to clean the roof on my East Orange property?

runs.v: No. Cleaning is maintenance, not construction, so it needs no construction permit under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

faqs.q: How do you clean the roof on an East Orange multi-family building without harming the landscaping or drains?

runs.v: The crew pre-wets and covers plantings, limits overspray in narrow side yards, and clears gutters and downspouts during the rinse so dead growth drains away.

faqs.q: How often does a roof need cleaning in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: North-facing slopes under heavy canopy regrow moss fastest. Rather than relying on annual inspections, follow the NRCA advice to inspect a roof twice a year, spring and fall, and clean when growth returns.

faqs.q: How much does roof cleaning and moss removal cost in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Roof cleaning costs $300–$1,050, about $675 for a 1,500-square-foot home, per This Old House; moss prevention adds $150–$250.

faqs.q: How much does gutter cleaning cost in New Jersey?

runs.v: It is usually priced by gutter length and house height, so a three-story walk-up costs more than a one-story home. Newark Quality Roofing clears gutters during a roof-cleaning rinse, so ask for both on one free estimate.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: As a rule of thumb, once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, replacement usually beats repair. As code, N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires a permit to repair more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months on buildings other than detached one- and two-family homes.

faqs.q: What is the average lifespan of a roof in New Jersey?

runs.v: Asphalt shingle roofs typically last about 20–30 years in New Jersey and slate far longer; moss and algae left in place shorten both.
